A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same RepExp research. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite additions and layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original inference-time selection, token-level generation, and RL post-training experiments on mathematical reasoning and coding tasks in Sections 4–5 and Appendices B–C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds protein-sequence selection results, response-likelihood analyses, and a computational-overhead estimate.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1, the RL exploration bonus, and the token-level logit modification are unchanged. The protein application uses the same selection procedure with ESMC embeddings. The new group-awareness footnote reiterates the covariance reset already described in v1 Section 5.

E1.justification: New Section 4.3 extends evaluation from mathematical reasoning and coding to unconditional protein-sequence generation and selection, a substantially different domain and task. Existing coverage is retained; the new likelihood analyses reuse MATH and GSM8K.

E2.justification: Corresponding experiments retain their comparator sets: random selection, vanilla generation, and the RL comparisons with GRPO, Unlikeliness, and the base model. The protein experiment reuses random selection, while the likelihood analysis uses already evaluated base and GRPO models.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a protein evaluation protocol with 2,048 ESM3-open sequences per masked prompt, lengths 64–916 in increments of four, and ESMFold plausibility requiring both pLDDT and pTM above 0.8. RF7 also introduces sampling one response per MATH test question and scoring its base-model likelihood. Existing experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: New RF7 and Appendix D directly investigate the central beyond-sharpening question through response-likelihood distributions on MATH and GSM8K. Appendix C adds a computational-overhead analysis. Existing representation ablations, model-strength analyses, hardness analyses, and sampler comparisons are retained.

E5.justification: v1 Figure 7 identifies the hardness-analysis intervals as 95% paired bootstrap confidence intervals. v2 retains that analysis in Figure 10 but drops this statistical description. Existing five-trial inference estimates, three-seed RL evaluations, and standard-error reporting otherwise remain unchanged.

E6.justification: New protein results report average samples-to-correct of 240.3 for random selection versus 6.7 for RepExp, a 35.9x ratio, and up to 56.9x verifier-efficiency improvement in Figure 8. Figures 9/12 add lower base-model likelihoods for RepExp responses. Appendix C reports 0.73x GRPO throughput, or 1.37x time per step. Existing math/code results are unchanged.

T1.justification: The elliptical-bonus definitions, token-generation equations, and Proposition B.1 with its covariance derivation and proof are unchanged. Moving the discussion of Foster et al. from a footnote into the main text adds no theoretical result.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal efficiency and diversity-collapse claims remain unchanged. Section 1.1 adds an explicit contribution claim that RepExp induces responses that look substantially more novel under the base model, modestly extending the stated findings.

C2.justification: v2 interprets lower base-model likelihoods as evidence against mere sharpening and extends the practical-applicability discussion to protein selection, explicitly acknowledging proxy verification. Appendix C newly explains the source of RL overhead and discusses hypothetical ways to avoid it.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 specifies the protein generation, embedding, and structure-prediction models. Appendix C newly documents reference-model feature computation and its extra forward pass. The reproducibility statement adds Weights & Biases usage and clarifies code coverage; the existing code address and hyperparameter tables remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Hayes et al. (2025), Lin et al. (2023), and ESM Team (2024) for the protein application, plus Karan and Du (2025) as inspiration for the likelihood analysis. The broader related-work discussion and positioning in Section 6 and Appendix A remain unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds Section 4.3, RF7, Appendix D, and a reproducibility statement, alongside localized wording corrections and explanatory edits. Most existing prose and the overall methodological narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 adds the protein plot and likelihood histograms in Figures 8, 9, and 12. Figure 7 becomes a single-panel display; its hardness analysis remains in the appendix. Existing appendix Figures 8/9 become 10/11, with localized relocation and text wrapping. Tables remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The protein experiment and MATH/GSM8K likelihood analyses provide useful additional evidence, while Appendix C makes computational costs clearer. These gains are qualified: protein success uses structural-confidence proxies, and lower likelihood alone does not establish novel correct reasoning. The established results remain intact. Overall, the additions outweigh the small reporting regression from losing the retained hardness plot’s 95% paired-bootstrap interval description.
